en-US.wiki.WKCargo_Intro.text-intro-1: Train Stations load Cargo for transportation, and with these new buildings, you can now pack, transport, store, and unpack cargo on your own accord. The Cargo Belt moves around 18x as much as a Space Belt of the same length: every slot on it holds a whole package of 360 shapes rather than a single shape. A Train Station only holds a few cargo containers, and once it fills, everything feeding it backs up until a train arrives to accept more cargo.
en-US.wiki.WKCargo_Intro.text-intro-2: Train Loaders and unloaders will accept and unload Cargo to and from Cargo Packagers, Cargo Unpackagers, Cargo Stores, or Cargo Belts directly.
en-US.wiki.WKCargo_Intro.text-robot: We're going to need a crane to move all these boxes...
en-US.wiki.WKCargo_Belt.text-intro-1: <gl>Cargo Belts</gl> carry <gl>Cargo</gl> containers, and will transport them to the next location. <gl>Cargo Belts</gl> may hold up to 4 <gl>Cargo</gl> at a time. <gl>Cargo Belts</gl> are created in paths just like any other belt - corners are placed automatically for you.
en-US.wiki.WKCargo_Belt.text-intro-2: A cargo belt will not send its cargo to a Space Belt, Space Pipe, or platform. Cargo needs to be unpackaged using a Cargo Unpackager to be able to use the contents of the Cargo.
en-US.wiki.WKCargo_Packager.text-intro-1: Cargo Packagers accept raw shapes and packs them into Cargo - the same type of container that a Train Station accepts, so wagon capacity research applies to both. Cargo Packagers accept shapes on each Space Level individually and outputs cargo on the same level. Cargo can only contain a single shape, so feeding two competing shapes will stall the Cargo Packagers. The Fluid Cargo Packager does the same thing, but accepts input from a Space Pipe. Fluid cargo counts blobs rather than litres, like the Fluid Loader.
en-US.wiki.WKCargo_Packager.text-robot: Be careful transporting that fluid, we don't want to have to write up a code violation.
en-US.wiki.WKCargo_Unpackager.text-intro-1:
<gl>Cargo Unpackagers</gl> open <gl>Cargo</gl> and put the contents back onto a <gll:WKIslands_SpaceBelts>Space Belt</gll> or into a <gll:WKFluids_SpacePipes>Space Pipe</gll>.

<gll:WKTrains_TrainStations>Train Stations</gll> will accept <gl>Cargo</gl> directly while <gll:WKTrains_TrainStations>Wagon Unloaders</gll> may unload to <gll:WKIslands_SpaceBelts>Space Belt</gll>, or <gll:WKFluids_SpacePipes>Space Pipes</gll> as normal, but, they may also unload to a <gll:WKCargo_Belt>Cargo Belt</gll>, <gll:WKCargo_Store>Cargo Store</gll>, or <gl>Cargo Unpackager</gl>.

An unpackager takes a new container only once it has emptied the last, so the belt behind it backs up and waits until there is room downstream.
en-US.wiki.WKCargo_Unpackager.text-robot: Didn't you just put them in this box? And now we are taking stuff out of it? Amateur.
en-US.wiki.WKCargo_Store.text-intro-1: Cargo Stores can buffer up to 75 containers, 25 on each floor. Place one between a Cargo Packager and a Train Station to ensure production factories run at maximum capacity, and to ensure that Trains on long routes will have items to come back to without needing to wait for production. Or, use them at the end of track to buffer cargo in a holding store for future trains or factories to receive when they need it.
en-US.wiki.WKCargo_Store.text-robot: Seventy-five containers?! What are you hoarding in there!!
